problem: The definition of thermodynamics appears twice in almost the same words (lead: 'studies energy, matter and their changes'; Section 1: 'the study of energy, matter and the changes they undergo'). A student on a phone reads the opening twice and gains nothing the second time.
fix: Keep the full definition in Section 1 only; open the lead with the two viewpoints, e.g. 'A sample can be described molecule by molecule, or by bulk quantities you can measure.'

problem: 'About 10¹⁹ molecules' per cubic centimetre is loose. At room conditions the count is nearer 2.5×10¹⁹ per cm³, so a student who meets the Loschmidt number later may think the notes were wrong by a factor of two or three.
fix: Write 'about 2.5×10¹⁹ molecules per cubic centimetre near room temperature and pressure (an order of magnitude of 10¹⁹)'

problem: 'The two views do not give different thermodynamics' is vague. A student may not see whether this means different laws, different results or different properties.
fix: Say: 'The two views do not give different answers. Both describe the same state; the microscopic view follows molecules, the macroscopic view measures their averages.'

problem: The phrase 'microscopic-type molecular quantity' is a new, undefined label. The chapter never defines 'microscopic-type', so the student cannot tell whether this is a formal classification or a description.
fix: Say plainly: 'An average over molecules in a tiny volume is a statistical molecular quantity, so it belongs to the microscopic view; tank pressure is a bulk property read by a gauge, so it is macroscopic.'
